subject.title: [Bug]: exec tool treats subprocess nonzero exit codes as tool failures, masking stdout and exit-code semantics

question: Should completed exec results with nonzero exit codes be nonfatal agent results by default across embedded-agent and isolated cron surfaces?
rationale: Current main has two competing semantics: the exec runner preserves nonzero exits as completed output, while downstream agent and cron state still use any nonzero exitCode as a generic failure signal.

options.title: Make normal exec nonzero nonfatal
options.body: Update the shared classifier and cron/embedded-agent tests so completed exec exit codes preserve stdout/stderr and diagnostics without setting tool failure state.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in semantics
options.body: Keep the current default but add a documented accepted-exit or nonfatal-exit policy surface, accepting more configuration and upgrade complexity.

options.title: Keep failure semantics
options.body: Document wrapper-based workarounds and close the bug as intentional, accepting that cron jobs using exit codes semantically must force exit 0.

recommendation.title: Make normal exec nonzero nonfatal
recommendation.body: Update the shared classifier and cron/embedded-agent tests so completed exec exit codes preserve stdout/stderr and diagnostics without setting tool failure state.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice sits in the shared tool-result classifier and adjacent cron recovery behavior tied to this history.
